## Preferences

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-roles.sh from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Use names that say what a thing is.** Use a name that says what the thing does or is, rather than a role word such as `manager`, `helper`, `service`, or `provider`. [`coding/use-names-that-say-what-a-thing-is.md`]
- **Name ports for capabilities and adapters for implementations.** Use the capability's own name for a port, with no `Port`, `Service`, or `Interface` suffix, and the concrete implementation's name for an adapter. [`coding/name-ports-for-capabilities-and-adapters-for-implementations.md`]
- **Name TypeScript files without type-tag suffixes.** Use the thing's own name for a TypeScript file and let the directory carry its role, with no `.port.ts`, `.service.ts`, `.provider.ts`, `.use-case.ts`, `.interface.ts`, or `.handler.ts` suffix. [`coding/name-typescript-files-without-type-tag-suffixes.md`]
- **Keep comment lines within the formatter's print width.** Keep comment-only lines within the formatter's print width by hand, since neither `CSharpier` nor `oxfmt` wraps comments; a single unbreakable token (a URL, a path) may overflow, and so may a tool directive, which its tool reads from that one line. [`tools/keep-comment-lines-within-the-formatters-print-width.md`]
- **Name a double for what it is.** Use `Fake*` for a behavioural fake, `InMemory*` for an in-memory implementation of a storage or transport port (the application-owned type that names a capability), and `Inline*` for a synchronous stand-in for an async dispatcher, rather than `Mock*` or `Stub*`. [`tests/name-a-double-for-what-it-is.md`]
- **Keep test doubles in the test support folder.** Use one support folder for test doubles: `TestSupport/<Feature>/` in a .NET test project, and a lower-case `support/` folder inside a TypeScript test tree. [`tests/keep-test-doubles-in-the-test-support-folder.md`]
- **Build the test subject in one factory method.** Use a private `CreateUseCase()` factory in each test class to build the subject under test. [`tests/build-the-test-subject-in-one-factory-method.md`]
- **Keep frontend tests in a top-level tests folder.** Use a top-level `tests/` directory at the frontend root that mirrors the source tree, rather than `__tests__/` folders or specs beside source files. [`tests/keep-frontend-tests-in-a-top-level-tests-folder.md`]
- **Keep TypeScript package tests at the package root.** Use a top-level `test/` or `tests/` directory at the package root for a TypeScript API's or library's tests. [`tests/keep-typescript-package-tests-at-the-package-root.md`]
- **Keep dotnet tests in a sibling tests project.** Use the conventionally named sibling test project (`*.Tests`) for .NET tests. [`tests/keep-dotnet-tests-in-a-sibling-tests-project.md`]
- **Promote injected dependencies to private readonly properties.** Use constructor property promotion for injected dependencies, `private readonly` by default and `protected readonly` only for a real inheritance reason. [`backend/promote-injected-dependencies-to-private-readonly-properties.md`]
- **Name a port pair inject and provide.** Use `injectX` and `provideX`, in that order, for a port's exported pair, and keep `useX` for concrete composables. [`frontend/name-a-port-pair-inject-and-provide.md`]
- **Name a composable file after its function.** Use the exported function's camelCase name as the composable's file name. [`frontend/name-a-composable-file-after-its-function.md`]
